item.title: 13 dead, two critical following Kassam Pass crash
item.description: Bodies of accident victims at Kassam Pass, Okuk Highway (Supplied) A fatal road accident at Kassam Pass along the Okuk Highway this morning has claimed 13 lives, including men, women and children.
item.content:encoded:
Bodies of accident victims at Kassam Pass, Okuk Highway (Supplied)

A fatal road accident at Kassam Pass along the Okuk Highway this morning has claimed 13 lives, including men, women and children.

Eastern Highlands Provincial Police Commander, Chief Superintendent Albert Beli, says the vehicle was travelling from Kagua in Southern Highlands Province to Lae when it crashed at around 4:30 am.

Thirteen of the 15 people on board were killed, while the two survivors were admitted to EBC Kassam Rural Hospital in critical condition.

Beli says several fatal road accidents have occurred in recent weeks as more people travel ahead of the Christmas and New Year holidays.

“There have been several accidents in recent weeks, raising concerns about road safety and the need for drivers to take extra precautions to protect their passengers,” Beli said.

PPC Beli is urging vehicle owners to remind their drivers to take responsibility, observe speed limits and take regular breaks, stressing that passenger safety must always come before making money.

“I urge drivers not to rush when carrying passengers. Their safety must come first, do not put money ahead of the lives of the people you are carrying.”

“I also urge drivers to be extra cautious during this period of heavy rainfall, as fog can affect visibility along the highway, particularly when travelling in the early hours,” Beli said.

Beli has expressed his deepest condolences to the families of those who lost their lives, describing the incident as deeply saddening.

He has also thanked highway patrol officers and nearby community members who assisted at the accident scene and helped recover the bodies.

Due to the high number of fatalities, the bodies of the deceased were transported to Lae under Highway Patrol escort.

item.title: Government expects balanced 2027 budget exceeding K30 billion
item.description: The Marape-Rosso Government is anticipating a balanced budget exceeding K30 billion when Parliament reconvenes for its November session next week. Prime Minister James Marape said the 2027 Budget will be tabled by Treasurer Joseph Lelang.
item.content:encoded:
The Marape-Rosso Government is anticipating a balanced budget exceeding K30 billion when Parliament reconvenes for its November session next week.

Prime Minister James Marape said the 2027 Budget will be tabled by Treasurer Joseph Lelang.

He made this known on Monday before departing for the World Leaders Economic Meeting in China.

The country will know its financial plan for next year when Parliament reconvenes next Tuesday for its November session.

According to tradition, the Budget lock-up will take place, where the Treasurer and National Planning Minister will outline the Government's key priorities for 2027, including sector allocations.

Prime Minister James Marape met with his Cabinet on Monday to go through the country's financial plan.

He indicated that the Government is looking at tabling a balanced budget.

The 2026 Budget was K30.9 billion, with revenue projected at K29.3 billion, focusing strongly on security, essential services and economic growth.

According to the Prime Minister, Treasurer Joseph Lelang will present the 2027 Budget to the country for the first time.

The Budget will exceed K30 billion under the Government's 13-year fiscal consolidation plan, advanced by former Treasurer Ian Ling-Stuckey.

Mr Marape reminded the people that the country is experiencing tough times and urged them to live within their means.

item.title: PPC Yangen calls for stronger police checks at Kumul border
item.description: The Kumul Border Check Point along the Enga–Western Highlands boundary. (Supplied-Clinton Kopyato) Police officers manning the Kumul Border Check Point along the Enga–Western Highlands provincial boundary have been urged to strongly enforce against traffic offences, illegal firearms and the smuggling of alcohol into the province.
item.content:encoded:
The Kumul Border Check Point along the Enga–Western Highlands boundary. (Supplied-Clinton Kopyato)

Police officers manning the Kumul Border Check Point along the Enga–Western Highlands provincial boundary have been urged to strongly enforce against traffic offences, illegal firearms and the smuggling of alcohol into the province.

In a media release, Enga Provincial Police Commander, Acting Superintendent Daniel Yangen, issued this call during a visit to the checkpoint on November 14.

He called on officers to exercise their police powers and take firm action against motorists driving without licences, operating unregistered or unroadworthy vehicles, driving under the influence of alcohol and carrying excess passengers.

He also directed officers to conduct thorough inspections of vehicles travelling through the checkpoint to detect illegal firearms and smuggled beer.

"No vehicle is to pass through without a proper check. We must stop illegal firearms and smuggled beer from entering Enga. These items are fuelling tribal fights, crime and drunk and disorderly behaviour in our communities," PPC Yangen said.

PPC Yangen also acknowledged the need for a properly established police station at the Kumul Border Check Point, saying it would improve police command, accommodation, exhibit storage, officer welfare and border security.

Meanwhile, he encouraged young people in the area, particularly Grade 10 and Grade 12 school leavers, to prepare their documents and apply for regular police recruitment when applications are announced.

He said eligible applicants would be considered for recommendation, provided they meet the required recruitment standards and followed the proper application process.

PPC Yangen also commended officers stationed at the checkpoint for their commitment and urged them to maintain discipline and integrity in carrying out their duties.

item.title: Air Niugini fares to increase
item.description: Air Niugini Chief Executive Officer, Allan Milne (NBC News) The travelling public have been advised to expect airfare increases at this time.
item.content:encoded:
Air Niugini Chief Executive Officer, Allan Milne (NBC News)

The travelling public have been advised to expect airfare increases at this time.

Due to ongoing global tensions and supply chain disruptions impacting the global aviation industry which relies heavily on fuel, Air Niugini has confirmed that its airfares will start increasing this Friday, 2Oth November.

The increase in costs including airport, air navigation, security charges and especially fuel requires a nine percent increase domestic base fares which means there will be a K250 increase on all domestic fares.

The flag carrier's Chief Executive Officer Allan Milne told this newsroom though it is unfortunate, it is a decision by the airline's board and management due to the substantial increase in the price of Jet A1 fuel since February, this year.

Mr Milne says the airline has delayed passing domestic fare increases for almost two years, but it is no longer sustainable.

Mr Milne however expressed gratitude to the national government for the subsidy relief assistance over the last few months which has greatly pushed back domestic price pressures.

Meantime, the airline CEO says monthly reviews will be done and recommendations made to the Air Niugini Board to reflect any further changes.

item.title: Madang Government assists maintenance at old school
item.description: Governor Ramsey Pariwa handing over the dummy cheque to the head teacher of Kamba Primary School and board members (NBC News) Kamba Primary School in Madang District will now carry out some basic maintenance works on its run-down classrooms, following financial assistance of K50, 000 from Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa's discretionary funds.
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ramsey Pariwa handing over the dummy cheque to the head teacher of Kamba Primary School and board members (NBC News)

Kamba Primary School in Madang District will now carry out some basic maintenance works on its run-down classrooms, following financial assistance of K50, 000 from Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa's discretionary funds.

Kamba is a pioneer school in ward 4 of the Ambenob Local Level Government.

Governor Pariwa travelled to the school last week and presented a dummy cheque of K50, 000 and the remittance advice, confirming that the funds have been deposited into the school's bank account.

Board Chairman of the school, Kevin Daur, said the school was established mainly to serve the rural communities in the hinterlands of central Ambenob LLG.

Mr Daur, said the school's infrastructures which were built by the colonial administration had gone through wear-and-tear over the years, plus neglect by relevant authorities obviously sees most of the facilities old and in run-down state.

The Head Teacher, Sibung Bawe, was present with the PCA Chairman, Wayne Paman, and a vocal community leader Bagen Dage to greet Governor Pariwa and his officers.

On behalf of the school management, Mr Bawe expressed his gratitude and appreciation to Governor Pariwa for the very worthwhile financial assistance.

The PCA Chairman, in expressing his appreciation and on behalf of the Kamba community, remarked that such assistance had not been provided to them for a long while.

"We are so thankful to you Governor Pariwa. You really have the heart and time for the community in need and children of Kamba will greatly benefit from this generous assistance," he said.

Pariwa whilst chatting with the locals explained to them his jurisdiction on supporting tertiary and secondary schools.

However, he stated that upon getting numerous requests from primary schools he is using his discretionary funds to support them a little on improving their infrastructures so children can enjoy a conducive learning environment.

item.title: BSP opens Sub-Branch in Walume, Southern highlands
item.description: The new BSP Sub-Branch in Walume Imbonggu district was opened on Friday 13th November to the public in Imbonggu and Southern Highlands. It will provide banking services such as deposits, withdrawals, account openings and digital banking (NBC News) People in Imbonggu district, Southern Highlands province, will no longer have to spend extra money traveling to Mendi or Mt Hagen just to access basic b
item.content:encoded:
The new BSP Sub-Branch in Walume Imbonggu district was opened on Friday 13th November to the public in Imbonggu and Southern Highlands. It will provide banking services such as deposits, withdrawals, account openings and digital banking (NBC News)

People in Imbonggu district, Southern Highlands province, will no longer have to spend extra money traveling to Mendi or Mt Hagen just to access basic banking services.

The BSP Walume Sub-Branch in Walume is now providing banking services closer to communities in the district, reducing the travel time, costs and especially their security faced by customers who previously had to travel long distances to access a BSP branch.

For families, small businesses, public servants and other customers in Imbonggu, the service means more of their money can now be kept for their daily needs instead of being spent on transport and other costs associated with travelling to Mendi or Mt Hagen.

BSP Group General Manager Retail, Ronesh Dayal, says bringing banking services closer to the people is part of BSP’s commitment to supporting growing communities.

"The Walume Sub-Branch is not just a traditional bank branch, it is part of BSP's vision for the branch of the future where banking is easier, customer wait times are shorter, and customers are increasingly in control of how they bank," stressed Mr Dayal.

" Walume and Imbonggu are growing with businesses, government services, and communities contributing towards the district's development, and reliable financial services are an important part of that growth."

Mr. Dayal adds the service will also allow customers to access digital banking services, including Mobile banking, Internet banking, and Wantok Wallet.

Imbonggu District CEO Paul Kereme has assured BSP that the people of Imbonggu will look after the banking services now available in the district.

He says the community must take ownership of the service and ensure it continues to benefit the people of Imbonggu.

" We must look after this banking services that is now made available at our doorstep. Many public servants, small entrepreneurs and other members of the public in Imbonggu and Southern Highlands will benefit from this bank and it will only be operational and serve us if we look after this asset in our district," says IDFA CEO Mr. Kereme.

Minister for Justice and Attorney General, Pila Niningi, has also welcomed the service, while urging people to act decently and behave properly when using the BSP facilities.

He says customers must respect the banking staff, the facility and other customers to ensure the service remains available to the community.

The Walum service is BSP’s fourth service point in Southern Highlands, adding to its existing presence in Pangia, Moro and Mendi.

And across the Highlands Region, BSP has 300 staffs that supports customers through 17 branches, 60 ATMs, 2,500 plus eftpos terminals and 140 agents.

The BSP Walume Sub Branch will provide services like account openings, deposits, withdrawals, and digital banking.

item.title: Masi calls for easier cross-border access for emergency patients
item.description: West Sepik Provincial Health Authority Chief Executive Officer Stanley Masi is calling on Papua New Guinea and Indonesia to make cross-border medical referrals easier, particularly for emergency patients who may need to travel at night or do not have passports. Mr Masi made the call during the signing of a Memorandum of Agreement between West Sepik PHA, Dian Harapan Hospital, Provita Hospital and
item.content:encoded:
West Sepik Provincial Health Authority Chief Executive Officer Stanley Masi is calling on Papua New Guinea and Indonesia to make cross-border medical referrals easier, particularly for emergency patients who may need to travel at night or do not have passports.

Mr Masi made the call during the signing of a Memorandum of Agreement between West Sepik PHA, Dian Harapan Hospital, Provita Hospital and the National Department of Health in Jayapura on Thursday, November 12.

While the agreement provides a pathway for patients from West Sepik to access specialised diagnosis and treatment in Jayapura, Mr Masi said the real test would be how both countries manage emergency referrals.

"In the future, we might move our patients at night. We expect our patients to come over at night. Those arrangements, both countries, Indonesia and Papua New Guinea, must be prepared to get emergency referrals coming in at night." Mr Masi said.

He said many patients in West Sepik do not have passports, while hospitals and border officials are not always equipped to process travel documents quickly when urgent medical attention is needed.

To address this, Mr Masi proposed that the two countries consider introducing a Traditional Border Crossing Card [TBC] for patients who need medical treatment across the border.

"And if we are not able to have the facilities that can provide passports and all these, I would really appreciate if the team from Indonesia and Papua New Guinea can work together to develop something like a Traditional Border Crossing Card for our patients. They do not need a passport to come here. Let's make something that is critical for them" Mr Masi said.

He said such an arrangement would help patients access urgent medical services without being delayed by passport requirements.

"This MOA also covers the people living along the border. People from Telefomin, Vanimo-Green, and from the Indonesia side, they must also go to Vanimo, West Sepik and other hospitals in Papua New Guinea to get the service."

The call was made in the presence of senior officials from both countries, including Deputy Secretary for Health Dr Dora Lenturut, West Sepik Governor Tony Wouwou, Provincial Administrator Jacob Areman and Papua Province Deputy Governor Aryoko Rumaropen.

The agreement is based on the Cross Border Medical Access Framework signed by the governments of Papua New Guinea and Indonesia in 2024, and the National Referral Guidelines launched by the National Department of Health in 2025.

Mr Masi said the next step was for technical teams from both countries to work out practical arrangements for night referrals and the proposed border crossing card, ensuring patients are not delayed from receiving treatment because of paperwork or the time of day.

item.title: MBP child and family protection council to exercise their powers
item.description: Milne Bay Province Child and Family Services Council members with the Minister for Community Development Youth and Religion Hon Jason Peter seated in front with Acting Provincial Administrator and Council Chair Sharon Mua, NOCFS Executives and Council members. (NBC News) The National Office of Child and Family Services has called on the members of the newly established Milne Bay Provincial Child a
item.content:encoded:
Milne Bay Province Child and Family Services Council members with the Minister for Community Development Youth and Religion Hon Jason Peter seated in front with Acting Provincial Administrator and Council Chair Sharon Mua, NOCFS Executives and Council members. (NBC News)

The National Office of Child and Family Services has called on the members of the newly established Milne Bay Provincial Child and Family Services Council to work together with all four districts in the province to implement the Lukautim Pikinini Act 2015. ‎ ‎Director of the National Office for Child and Family Services Jerry Wap made this call recently and described Milne Bay as a peaceful province but stressed that it does not necessarily rule out the fact that not every child is safe and protected.

‎"Even in a peaceful province, our children are not always safe. We still have children who are beaten in homes, girls marrying at young age, children who drop out of school and without home, children who are neglected by divorce, children with disability who are beaten and forgotten and teenage mothers who need help and not judgment."Wap said.

‎Mr Wap emphasized that child protection is not about taking children away from families but by providing necessary support to help families raise healthy and well -protected children. ‎ ‎Meanwhile, Milne Bay Provincial Administrator and Chair of the Child and Family Services Council, Sharon Mua said the Council plays a very critical role in ensuring the safety and welfare of the children across the province.

‎"This Council will serve a vital bridge between government, communities and families. It will play a pivotal role in safeguarding our children from abuse and neglect, providing essential family support services and to coordinate Provincial policies with national strategies to deliver effective social services for our people", Ms Mua said. ‎ ‎She challenged her fellow council members to uphold the sacred duty entrusted to them by carrying out their duties with integrity, compassion and commitment. ‎ ‎The Provincial Child and Family Services Council comprises of representatives from key government sectors and community organizations, with the provincial Administrator as chair.

‎Its membership includes the Police, Magisterial services, Education, the Pastors and Ministers fraternity, Church agencies and Women groups. ‎
